questions.question: Literature generally refers to ________.
options: B. A body of written works or texts

questions.question: The following are examples of non-fictional literature EXCEPT ________.
options: C. The Lion and the Jewel

questions.question: The following are benefits of literature EXCEPT ________.
options: B. It helps one understand different aspects of life
C. It automatically helps one gain political office

questions.question: Which of the following normally comes first in the organization of a plot?
In a literary work, when an idea is emphasized by stating it again, the device used is ________.
A technique whereby a supernatural being is suddenly introduced to resolve a crisis in drama is called ________.
Prose is usually written in ________.
Another name for enjambment in poetry is ________.
When a literary work creates mental pictures in the mind of the reader, the device used is ________.
A short story in which animals are given human qualities and which often teaches a moral lesson is called a ________.

Use the passage below to answer Questions 11–15.

The teacher's stomach made a grunting noise like the sliding movement of a snake. His intestines protested the long abstinence imposed on them. Simultaneously, Nebe yawned. A long-protracted yawn which brought tears to his eyes. As he put out his hands to wipe the tears, he was stopped right in his tracks.

The angle of narration is ________.
In the passage in Question 11, the comparison of the stomach's grunting noise to the sliding movement of a snake is a ________.
From the passage in Question 11, Nebe is most likely a ________.
The mood in the passage in Question 11 is mainly one of ________.
The most suitable title for the passage in Question 11 is ________.
The following are major genres of literature EXCEPT ________.
The following are characteristics of poetry EXCEPT ________.
options: A. It is written in lines
B. Its lines may be arranged in stanzas
C. It is arranged mainly in scenes
D. It may make use of rhyme

questions.question: Drama is a form of literature intended primarily for performance before an audience.
The particular choice of words used by a writer is known as ________.
The central message or main idea conveyed by a literary work is its ________.
The following are types of drama EXCEPT ________.
A play characterized by serious subject matter and a tense atmosphere is generally a ________.
The literary device involving an interruption of the present action to show an earlier event is called ________.
The classical dramatic principle that restricts the events of a play to approximately twenty-four hours is the unity of ________.
The artistic and imaginative expression of human thoughts and feelings in rhythmic language is called ________.
Which of the following is NOT a type of poetry?
An indirect reference to the Bible, history, mythology or another literary work is called ________.
A figure of speech in which an absent person, idea or inanimate object is directly addressed is called ________.
The placing together of two apparently contradictory terms is called ________.
"The boy is so strong that he got a broken head in a fight" is best regarded as an example of ________.
A character who opposes the main character in a literary work is called the ________.
The main character in a literary work is known as the ________.
A poem written to mourn the death of a person is called an ________.
The sequence of events in a literary work is known as the ________.
The time and place in which the events of a literary work occur constitute its ________.
A comparison using "like" or "as" is called a ________.
Deliberate exaggeration for emphasis is known as ________.
The conversation between two or more characters in a play is called ________.
A long speech made by a character alone on stage revealing private thoughts is a ________.
A character who remains essentially unchanged throughout a literary work is generally called a ________ character.

essay.title: PAPER 2 - THEORY
essay.instruction: Answer four (4) questions. Question One is compulsory.

questions.question:
Write short notes on the following figures of speech:
(i) Personification
(ii) Metaphor
(iii) Simile
(iv) Symbolism
(v) Allusion. (2 marks each)

(a) Define Literature as a field of study. (2 marks)
(b) State four importance of Literature. (8 marks)

(a) Explain English Literature and Literature-in-English. (4 marks)
(b) State three differences between English Literature and Literature-in-English. (6 marks)

Write short notes on the following elements of drama:
(i) Theme
(ii) Plot
(iii) Dialogue
(iv) Characters
(v) Visual effect. (2 marks each)

With two examples each, explain:
(i) Fictional literature
(ii) Non-fictional literature. (10 marks)
